key_bets: Wiffle-Ball confinement achieves loss reduction factor γ ≤ 0.1 at commercial plasma density (~10²¹ m⁻³), making Q_plasma ≈ 10.5 achievable
Virtual cathode (electrostatic potential well) can form and be sustained at reactor-relevant plasma densities without requiring the ~200,000 A electron supply rate calculated by Univ. Sydney (2019)
Bremsstrahlung radiation losses for a thermalized 20 keV D-T plasma at reactor density do not eliminate net energy gain
Park 2025 scaling laws (derived from WB-X/WB-8 PIC simulations) extrapolate validly across ~12× linear and ~10⁶× power scale-up to a 1.6 m cube, 4.5 T, 980 MW reactor
An MW-class electron beam injection system (60 keV, 1.3 kA, 78 MW total) can operate CW into a magnetic cusp with adequate beam-plasma coupling and component lifetime
A tritium breeding blanket achieving TBR > 1.1 can be engineered around the polyhedral coil geometry despite neutron shadowing from six coil faces
Superconducting coils for a 6-sided non-interlocking cusp geometry at 4.5 T steady-state are feasible and the modular assembly claim (easy assembly/disassembly) holds at reactor scale
eliminated_costs: No divertor system: cusp geometry naturally provides plasma exhaust at cusp points, eliminating the tokamak divertor design, replacement, and remote handling cost
Smaller, cheaper magnet system: magnets only confine electrons (not 20 keV ions at billion-particle densities), so magnetic energy density requirement is far lower than MFE tokamaks/stellarators
No interlocked TF coil remote maintenance: six non-interlocking modular coils enable straightforward manufacturing and assembly/disassembly versus fully remote tokamak maintenance
No burning-plasma physics infrastructure: device is not designed around self-sustaining burn, avoiding burn-control systems and associated engineering
Commercially sourced electron beam injectors (Leybold, Sciaky, Ferrotec) replace bespoke neutral beam / RF heating systems used in MFE H&CD
novel_costs: Polyhedral tritium breeding blanket engineered around six coil-face neutron shadows — ARIES-class analogue range $50–200M vs. ~$7M generic MFE formula, with concept-specific neutronics study required
MW-class electron beam injection system (78 MW total, 60 keV, 1.3 kA CW) with power supplies — override baseline ~$100M; structural recirculating load of ~29% at γ=0.1 (rising to 40–45%+ at γ=0.2)

Six independent superconducting cusp coils (4.5 T boundary field) with no shared load-bearing structure, each resisting magnetic pressure asymmetrically — custom coil forms required, override baseline ~$150M
Permanent structural recirculating power penalty from continuous CW e-beam drive (no ignition), compounding γ uncertainty by doubling beam demand if confinement degrades
Beam power supply electrical losses at 78 MW scale (~15% wall-plug loss at 85% efficiency = ~14 MW continuous) as a concept-specific recirculating load

risks.description: Loss reduction factor γ is an unvalidated free parameter in the Park 2025 scaling; the entire Q=10.5 projection rests on γ=0.1, and the coupled sweep shows γ=0.2 drives LCOE to net-negative

Virtual cathode formation at commercial plasma densities is disputed by Univ. of Sydney (2019) experiments finding 'little or no trace' of it; EMC2 has not published counter-experimental evidence, and invalidation collapses the entire physics basis
No energy conversion architecture specified — no blanket type, thermal cycle, coolant, or BOP — so net electric output is unknown within ±50% and no defensible LCOE can be constructed

Tritium breeding blanket design is TRL 1 with no neutronics study for the polyhedral cusp geometry; coil-face neutron shadowing may force higher Li-6 enrichment or thicker blankets, and $50–200M cost range is not reflected by standard MFE formulas
Physics scaling extrapolation spans ~12× linear and ~10⁶× power from WB-X sub-microsecond pulses to a 980 MW steady-state reactor; Park 2025 explicitly flags the gyroradius exponent as preliminary

Bremsstrahlung radiation balance is unresolved — Park 2025's thermalization assumption addresses Rider 1995 but implies a Maxwellian ion distribution that eliminates any direct-conversion advantage, a tension not acknowledged in the scaling paper

Superconducting coil design for 6-sided cusp geometry is TRL 3–4 with no published EMC2 work since reported 2012 start; mechanical loading under high-beta plasma pressure requires concept-specific engineering

EMC2 corporate transparency is low — no public results from WB-8 (2009–2012) or subsequent devices, and current activities have pivoted to the FPNS neutron source program with SHINE rather than a power reactor line

Structural recirculating power fraction (~29% at γ=0.1, rising to 40–45%+ at γ=0.2) is permanent because the e-beam must run continuously; this compounds γ uncertainty since doubling γ doubles beam power and halves Q_eng
O&M strategy, PFC lifetime under 14 MeV neutron flux, and capacity factor are entirely unspecified; modular coil replacement is a design claim, not a demonstrated maintenance plan

Tritium supply constraint: ~55 kg/yr required for a 980 MW fusion plant exceeds half of global tritium inventory (~25 kg), making on-site breeding mandatory — but no Polywell blanket design exists to provide it

MW-class electron beam injection at 78 MW total into a magnetic cusp at reactor plasma densities has not been demonstrated as an integrated system; beam-plasma coupling efficiency and long-term component lifetime under neutron/X-ray fluence are unproven
